title: Is There a Block With Sum Zero?

concept.title: Two equal prefix sums mean a zero block
body: Let `prefix[i]` be the sum of the first `i` numbers, with `prefix[0] = 0`. The sum of the block from position `i + 1` to `j` is `prefix[j] - prefix[i]`. So a block has sum zero exactly when **two prefix sums are equal**.

body.code:
seen = {0}          # the empty prefix
prefix = 0
for x in a:
    prefix += x
    if prefix in seen:
        return True       # a block with sum 0 ends here
    seen.add(prefix)

body: Starting the set with 0 handles blocks that begin at the first position: if the prefix itself becomes 0, it equals the empty prefix. Prefix sums combined with a hash set or map are one of the most useful tricks for block-sum questions.

statement: Is there a non-empty block of consecutive elements of the array whose sum is 0? Print `yes` or `no`.

examples.note: All blocks have a positive sum.

hints: The block between two equal prefix sums has sum 0.

explanation: Two equal prefix sums enclose a block with sum 0. A set of the prefix sums seen so far, starting with 0, detects this in one pass.
solution.complexity: Time O(n) on average, space O(n).

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

seen = {0}
prefix = 0
found = False
for x in a:
    prefix += x
    if prefix in seen:
        found = True
        break
    seen.add(prefix)
print("yes" if found else "no")
